note: Theory that is heard, not recited: find the three roots in the scale, hear their chords, then follow I-IV-V by ear in two different orders and backings. Works for any instrument, or none.

exercise.title: I, IV and V in G, by ear
exercise.focus: G major · roots G C D · I-IV-V-I by ear
exercise.why: Three chords carry thousands of songs; hearing which one is playing is the start of learning songs by ear.

sections.text: Build a chord on the 1st, 4th and 5th notes of a major scale and you have the three chords that carry most songs.
In G major, {{1}} is G, {{4}} is C and {{5}} is D. Tap each on the staff, then tap the chord built on it below.
Press Play: I, IV, V, I, one bar each. Say the numeral out loud on each change. I sounds like home, IV like stepping out, V like it is leaning back to I.
Same three chords in a different order, with a softer backing. Look away and name each chord as it arrives; then look to check. Done when you get a whole pass right.
